newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court fixes tax base for vets where services supplied.
newsitem.headline: Court fixes tax base for vets where services supplied.

text.p: The European Court of Justice interpreted Community rules governing tax assessment on Thursday and said veterinary surgical services are considered supplied where the vet's business is established.
If there is no one fixed establishment where services are supplied, a vet's permanent address or usual residence fixes the place of taxation on services.

The court said veterinary services fall within provision article 9(1) of the VAT directive, a general provision relating to services, and not article 9(2)(c) relating to work on movable tangible property.
"Sixth VAT directive - Article 9 - Supply of veterinary services"
Reference from the Gerechtshof te 's-Hertogenbosch (Netherlands) for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings between
Maatschap M.J.M. Linthorst, K.G.P. Pouwels and J. Scheres c.s.

on the interpretation of article 9 of the Sixth Council directive 77/388/EEc of 17 May on the harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to turnover taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment (OJ 1977 L 145, p. 1)

Article 9 of the Sixth Council directive 77/388/EEc of 17 May on the harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to turnover taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment must be interpreted as meaning that the place where the services principally and habitually carried out by a veterinary surgeon should be deemed to be supplied is the place where the supplier has established his business or has a fixed establishment from which the services are supplied or, in the absence of such a place of business or fixed establishment, the place where he has his permanent address or usually resides.
